candidates.original_title: Scaffolding Voluntary Summer Reading for Children in Grades 3 to 5: An Experimental Study
candidates.description: Providing children with books matched to their reading levels and interests plus teacher-led comprehension and fluency lessons and parent-supported reading activities improves summer-to-fall reading comprehension.
candidates.citation_sentence: In Kim and White ' s ( 2008 ) study and Kim ' s ( 2006 ) study, READS was implemented in a large and ethnically diverse suburban school district in the mid-Atlantic region.
candidates.notes: The multiple-strategy lesson condition was intended to replicate the prior procedure more closely, but the current study tested it in a different district and population. Effects were null overall, positive in high-poverty schools, and negative in moderate-poverty schools.

candidates.original_title: Effects of a Voluntary Summer Reading Intervention on Reading Achievement: Results From a Randomized Field Trial
candidates.description: A voluntary summer reading program providing students with books matched to their reading levels and interests, together with teacher scaffolding and parent support, improves subsequent reading comprehension.
candidates.citation_sentence: In Kim and White ' s ( 2008 ) study and Kim ' s ( 2006 ) study, READS was implemented in a large and ethnically diverse suburban school district in the mid-Atlantic region.
candidates.notes: The replication produced null overall effects, positive effects in high-poverty schools, and negative effects in moderate-poverty schools; the authors characterize this as nonreplication in the full sample but discuss positive effects in high-poverty schools.
